clue.text: Book accommodation with pleasant outlook

definitions.meaning: a novel by E. M. Forster bearing this title
lodging whose window looks out on a fine scene

explanation.definitionFit: Forster's 1908 novel takes its title from a lodging with a fine prospect, which is just what the second definition describes literally.

clue.text: Feel remorse about measure putting people off?

indicators.note: the word for feeling remorse wraps around the measure, so it sits about it

parts.note: to feel remorse is to repent
an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: Someone ponders whether a regret-inspiring policy measure is driving people away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repulsive or off-putting drives others back, as an insect deterrent does.

clue.text: Senior lord, English, covered in gold

indicators.note: the lord and English pieces are wrapped inside the heraldic word for gold

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: An elderly English peer is decked out in gold finery.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior here is the comparative of age: of greater years than another.

clue.text: Militarist friendly on meeting former enemy — many put off

parts.note: a warm welcome is a friendly one
taken as written

indicators.note: the word many is dropped off the end of the former enemy's name

parts.note: Germany, Britain's foe in two world wars
taken as written

explanation.surface: A belligerent type is friendly when meeting an old foe, which puts many people off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' removes MANY from GERMANY, leaving GER.
explanation.definitionFit: A militarist favours armed force, as does someone who stirs up conflicts between nations.

clue.text: Fusses when drunkard turns up outside party

indicators.note: the reversed drunkard sits outside, around the party
in a down clue turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drinker
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: There's a commotion when a drunk appears outside a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkard' suggests a person, but it only supplies letters; the fusses are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Commotions or bustles of agitation, noun plural like the clue word.

clue.text: Carbohydrate served up after a spring vegetable

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: in a down clue served up suggests the letters rise, read in reverse

parts.note: sugar is a carbohydrate

explanation.surface: Sugar is dished up after a spring vegetable at a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season of the vegetable, but it is a mineral spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Spears of this plant are a prized green eaten in spring.

clue.text: Jumper hanging in rain, dripping

indicators.note: the answer hangs within the run of letters across the next two words

explanation.surface: A sweater left hanging out in the rain is dripping wet.
explanation.definitionFit: This Madagascan lemur is famous for its huge leaps between trees.

clue.text: Alerts about soldiers in underground networks

indicators.note: the word for alerts goes about, around, the soldiers

parts.note: to alert is to warn
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Warnings are issued about troops in tunnel systems.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbits dig interconnected burrows below ground, and the word extends to any maze of passages.

clue.text: Doctor eats small amount when having a brandy

indicators.note: the doctor takes the small amount inside, as if eating it

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner
a rap is a tiny amount, as in not caring a rap

explanation.surface: A doctor nibbles a little while drinking brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian spirit distilled from grape pomace, a kind of brandy.

clue.text: Fastened bar to go round gym

indicators.note: the bar is made to encircle the gym letters

parts.note: a rod is a bar
PE, physical education, is gym class

explanation.surface: A bar is fixed in place encircling a gymnasium.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied up with cord or rope, past tense like the clue word.

clue.text: Spooner's hurried amendment to document is a pest

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped initial sounds, so the opening consonants of two words trade places

parts.note: sped means hurried
a rider is an added clause to a document or bill

explanation.surface: A rushed change to a legal text is a real nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping SP and R in SPED RIDER gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny mite that infests greenhouse and garden plants, a notorious horticultural pest.

clue.text: More sickly looking before brief time in port

indicators.note: the paler piece comes before the brief time in the answer

parts.note: paler means more wan, sicker in appearance
a mo is a moment, a brief time

explanation.surface: Someone looks more ill shortly before arriving in harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian capital is a major Mediterranean seaport.

clue.text: Something out of a tin it's right to eat?

parts.note: it, in the sense of sex appeal, is SA; the 's joins the pieces
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether it is proper to eat food straight from a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal (SA) is an old crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: This small oily fish is famously sold packed tightly in cans.

clue.text: Person managing business is a toff

parts.note: a toff is a posh gentleman, a gent

explanation.surface: The man running the company is a snob.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'toff' is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: A representative who acts on behalf of another and handles their affairs.

clue.text: Hoi polloi, those people fools!

parts.note: them refers to those people
asses are fools

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at the common crowd, calling them all idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi is Greek for 'the many', the ordinary people at large.

clue.text: Retire and take steps to become a singer

definitions.meaning: to withdraw from work, as an old horse is put out to pasture

definitions.text: take steps to become a singer
definitions.meaning: a grass is an informer, one who sings to the police, so this means set out to become one

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to stop working, like an old horse turned out to pasture; read literally it means setting out to become an informer, and an informer 'sings'.

clue.text: Urban dwelling? You may collect grant coming down to expensive part of country

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece comes down onto the second, which sits below it
the old word for you collects, gathers in, the word for grant

parts.note: thou is the archaic word for you
to own is to concede or grant
SE, the South East of England, is the priciest region

explanation.surface: Someone may land a housing grant on moving down to a costly region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grant' looks like money, but it is the verb meaning concede; south-east England is the costliest region of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A terraced residence in a city, as opposed to a country seat.

clue.text: One may let an old master go after a financial settlement

definitions.text: One may let an old master go after a financial settlement

parts.words: One may let an old master go after a financial settlement
parts.note: seems to describe a servant's employer paying off a former boss, but an old master is a classic painting sold once the price is agreed

explanation.definitionFit: A trader in pictures parts with classic paintings once a sale is agreed.

clue.text: Lousy performance by eight somewhere in the capital

parts.note: rotten means lousy, very bad
a rowing eight's effort is a row

explanation.surface: A rowing crew of eight puts in a terrible show in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is a riding track in London's Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic bridleway along the south side of Hyde Park, London.

clue.text: Egyptian place put in list

indicators.note: the word for put goes in the list

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
to set is to put

explanation.surface: An Egyptian location is added to a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nile delta town where the famous inscribed stone was found.

clue.text: Person looking after the weekend paper must be fully satisfied

parts.note: Sat, Saturday, is part of the weekend
the editor, Ed, looks after the paper

explanation.surface: The Saturday supplement's editor must be thoroughly content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' completes the picture of ED, the editor in charge of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Glutted or filled to the point of having had enough.

clue.text: Giving medicine to order as issued by one in charge of choir

definitions.meaning: administering a measured amount of a drug

definitions.text: order as issued by one in charge of choir
definitions.meaning: a choirmaster's command telling singers to perform

explanation.definitionFit: Administering drugs in measured amounts; split in two, the letters make a choirmaster's instruction to start singing.

clue.text: The main product that appears on the kitchen table?

definitions.text: The main product that appears on the kitchen table?

parts.words: The main product that appears on the kitchen table?
parts.note: the main is the ocean, so its product is a seasoning evaporated from seawater

explanation.definitionFit: Crystals obtained by evaporating seawater, used as a seasoning at meals.

clue.text: Where in Paris a mister keeps a secret lover

indicators.note: the mister holds the French word inside

parts.note: ou is French for where

explanation.surface: A Frenchman hides away a clandestine mistress somewhere in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A French word for a love affair, here the person loved, especially illicitly.

clue.text: River beginning to rise, flooding temporary home?

indicators.note: the first letter floods into the tent, entering it

parts.note: a tent is a temporary dwelling

indicators.note: the first letter of rise is taken

explanation.surface: A river starts to rise and floods a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of 'rise' goes inside TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: England's third-longest river flows through the Midlands.

clue.text: They make a great effort, the man asserts

parts.note: he refers to the man
avers means asserts

explanation.surface: A man claims that some people try very hard.
explanation.definitionFit: People who lift or haul with great exertion.

clue.text: A gee-gee runs round displaying violent behaviour

parts.note: a gee-gee is a child's word for a horse, GG
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A horse charges round a track, behaving violently.
explanation.walkthrough: AGGRO is British slang for aggressive trouble-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for hostile, aggressive conduct or trouble.

clue.text: Match items of clothing

parts.note: looks like a sports kit, but a match here is a marriage, so these are a bride's outfit and linens

explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes and linen assembled for her wedding.

clue.text: Physician dealt with wind and indigestion finally

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

indicators.note: the final letter of indigestion is used

explanation.surface: A doctor treated a patient's wind and indigestion at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealt with' is a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek medical writer whose theories dominated medicine for centuries.

clue.text: Orchestra so bad, messing it up completely

indicators.note: a messy performance scrambles these words into a new order

explanation.surface: A dreadful orchestra makes a total hash of the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messing it up' rearranges ORCHESTRA SO BAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying to everyone or everything equally, without exception.
